title: Protesters clash with police in Paris and across France over living costs and schools
seoTitle: Paris march against living costs and schools

tea.why: Students and workers are protesting over high living costs, rising prices, pension concerns, and dilapidated schools with staff shortages.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand better school funding, improved public services, higher wages, and action on the cost of living.
tea.changed: Oct 28: The French retail chamber reported severe revenue drops and thousands of damaged stores following nationwide protests.

summary: Mass demonstrations and marches took place across France, including Paris, drawing hundreds of thousands of participants amid widespread anger over soaring living costs, public services, and school funding. The movement, which originated from high school protests over staff shortages, has expanded to include trade unions and citizens calling for economic relief. While most marches began peacefully, clashes erupted near endpoints as some individuals threw projectiles, fireworks, and stones at police, who responded with tear gas, sound grenades, water cannons, and batons. Authorities reported numerous arrests, injuries among security personnel, and extensive property damage, vandalism, and looting in several cities. President Emmanuel Macron and government officials condemned the violence, while the Interior Ministry deployed tens of thousands of security personnel to maintain order and announced plans for further security measures ahead of upcoming weekend demonstrations.
demands: Action on the cost of living
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced a nationwide deployment of up to 70,000 police officers backed by water cannons and armored vehicles, reporting nearly 1,000 arrests. President Emmanuel Macron warned that those who destroy property or attack institutions will be prosecuted and punished.

crowd.text: The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000

arrests.text: Nationally, according to authorities, arrests have exceeded 1,200

deaths.text: A protester who took to the streets yesterday in Paris against the high cost of living died of cardiac arrest.

updates.text: Clashes erupted in Paris and other cities during nationwide demonstrations over living costs and schools, leading to numerous arrests.
The French retail chamber reported that inner-city store revenues dropped by 80 percent due to ongoing protests and civil unrest.
France prepared a 70,000-strong police deployment ahead of fresh nationwide protests scheduled for Saturday.
